Australia.intro: Australia is huge, and its seasons are the reverse of the northern hemisphere's. The tropical north (Cairns, the Great Barrier Reef) is best in the dry winter, while Sydney and Melbourne shine in spring and autumn.
seasons: September–November
Spring: warm in the south and still dry in the tropics — a great all-round time.
December–February
Summer: beach season in Sydney and Melbourne, but hot, wet and stormy in the far north.
June–August
Winter: the best time for the reef and the north; cool and crisp in the south.

Canada.intro: Canada's travel season is defined by its winters. Summer opens the Rockies' lakes and trails, autumn brings spectacular colours in Quebec, and winter is for skiing and carnivals.
seasons: June–September
Summer: warm days, open mountain roads and ice-free lakes.
Late September–October
Fall colours in Quebec and the east; quieter parks in the west.
December–March
Winter: skiing in Banff and Whistler, Quebec's Winter Carnival — and serious cold.

Colombia.intro: Colombia sits near the equator, so temperatures barely change through the year; altitude and rainfall make the difference. Medellín is spring-like all year, while Cartagena is hot and best in the dry season.
seasons: December–March
The main dry season across most of the country, and the busiest time on the Caribbean coast.
June–August
A shorter dry spell in the Andes; Medellín's flower festival in August.
April–May & October–November
The wettest months, with afternoon downpours.

Costa Rica.intro: Costa Rica has a dry season (verano) from December to April and a green season the rest of the year. The Pacific side — Guanacaste and Manuel Antonio — follows this pattern, while the Caribbean coast is often driest in September–October.
seasons: December–April
Dry season: sunny beaches and easy wildlife spotting, but the highest prices.
May–August
Green season: lush forests, morning sunshine and afternoon showers, with lower prices.
September–October
The wettest months on the Pacific side — but the best time for the Caribbean coast.

Croatia.intro: Croatia's Adriatic coast is a classic summer destination, but the shoulder seasons are its sweet spot: warm sea, sunshine and far fewer crowds in Split and Dubrovnik.
seasons: May–June
Warm, sunny and green, with long days and fewer cruise passengers.
July–August
Peak season: hot weather, the warmest sea and the biggest crowds.
September–October
Still-warm sea and harvest season — many travellers' favourite time.

Egypt.intro: Egypt is a winter-sun destination. Sightseeing in Cairo and Luxor is most comfortable from October to April, while the Red Sea coast stays warm enough for swimming much of the year.
seasons: October–April
Warm, sunny days ideal for temples, tombs and Nile cruises.
March–May & October–November
Perfect Red Sea weather: hot sun and warm water without extreme heat.
June–August
Intense heat, especially in Luxor and Aswan — sightsee at dawn.

Florida.intro: Florida is warm all year, but its seasons matter. Winter and spring are dry and pleasant; summer is hot and humid with daily thunderstorms, and August to October is peak hurricane season.
seasons: November–April
Dry season: sunny, mild and the most popular time to visit.
May–September
Hot, humid summer with afternoon storms — theme parks are busiest in school holidays.
August–October
Peak hurricane season: keep plans flexible and consider travel insurance.

Greece.intro: Greece's best weather runs from May to October. The islands are at their liveliest in summer, but late spring and early autumn bring warm seas, sunshine and smaller crowds — and on many islands, most hotels close in winter.
seasons: May–June
Warm and sunny, with wildflowers and fewer crowds — ideal for islands and sightseeing.
July–August
Peak season: hot (often 35°C+ in Athens), busy and pricey, with strong meltemi winds in the Cyclades.
September–October
Warm sea, harvest season and thinner crowds — the sweet spot for many travellers.

Hawaii.intro: Hawaii is warm all year, with only a few degrees between seasons. The real differences are rain (more in winter, especially on north and east shores), whales (December to April) and prices, which peak at Christmas and in summer.
seasons: April–June & September–October
The sweet spot: dry, sunny and cheaper, with fewer crowds.
December–March
Winter: whale season and big North Shore surf, but more rain and peak prices.
July–August
Summer: dry and calm seas, busy with family holidays.

Italy.intro: Italy's best seasons are spring and autumn, when it's warm enough for the coast but comfortable for walking around Rome, Florence and Venice. July and August are hot and crowded, and many locals take their holidays in mid-August.
seasons: April–June
Mild to warm, blossoms and long days — great for cities and the countryside.
July–August
Hot and busy, best for the beaches of the Amalfi Coast and Sicily.
September–October
Warm sea, grape harvests and fewer crowds.

Japan.intro: Japan has four distinct seasons. Spring cherry blossoms and autumn leaves are the most popular — and most crowded — times, while summer is hot and humid and winter brings snow to Hokkaido and crisp, sunny days to Tokyo.
seasons: Late March–May
Cherry blossoms and mild weather; Golden Week (late April–early May) is very busy.
June–August
June is the rainy season; July–August is hot, humid and festival-filled. Okinawa has typhoon risk.
October–November
Comfortable temperatures and autumn leaves — many people's favourite time.
December–February
Cold and dry in Tokyo and Kyoto; powder snow and the Snow Festival in Hokkaido.

Mexico.intro: Mexico's dry season from November to April is the best time for most of the country, from Cancún's beaches to Mexico City's museums. Summer brings rain and, on both coasts, hurricane risk from August to October.
seasons: November–April
Dry, sunny and warm — peak season on the beaches.
May–June
Hot before the rains; good value in the highlands.
July–October
Rainy season with afternoon storms; hurricane risk on the coasts, especially September.

New Zealand.intro: New Zealand's seasons are the reverse of Europe's and North America's. Summer (December to March) is best for hiking and beaches, while winter brings skiing around Queenstown.
seasons: December–March
Summer: warm, long days and the best hiking weather.
March–May
Autumn: settled weather, golden colours and fewer crowds.
June–September
Winter: ski season in Queenstown; cool and wet in Auckland.

Norway.intro: Norway offers two completely different trips: summer's midnight sun, fjords and hiking, or winter's northern lights, snow and dog-sledding above the Arctic Circle.
seasons: June–August
Midnight sun, mild weather and the best time for fjords and hiking.
September–March
Northern lights season in Tromsø and the Arctic.
December–January
Polar night in the north: no sunrise, but magical light and auroras.

Peru.intro: Peru's dry season (May to September) is the best time for the Andes, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Lima is the opposite: sunny in summer (December to April) and grey under coastal mist the rest of the year.
seasons: May–September
Dry season in the Andes: sunny days, cold nights and peak Machu Picchu crowds.
December–April
Rainy season in the mountains (the Inca Trail closes in February), but sunny summer in Lima.
April & October–November
Shoulder months with fewer crowds and mixed weather.

Portugal.intro: Portugal is one of Europe's sunniest countries. The mainland is best from spring to autumn, with beach weather on the Algarve from June to September, while Madeira stays mild all year.
seasons: April–June
Warm and sunny with fewer crowds — great for cities and coastal walks.
July–August
Hot, dry and busy: prime beach time on the Algarve.
September–October
Warm sea, grape harvests and quieter beaches.
November–March
Mild but wetter on the mainland; Madeira remains spring-like.

Scotland.intro: Scotland's weather is famously changeable, but late spring and summer bring the longest days — up to 18 hours of light — for exploring Edinburgh, the Highlands and Skye.
seasons: May–June
Long days, fewer midges and often the driest weather.
July–August
Warmest months and Edinburgh's festivals, but midges in the Highlands.
November–February
Short, dark days and storms — but cosy pubs and Hogmanay.

Spain.intro: Spain has a sunny climate, but it varies widely: Seville and Madrid get very hot in summer, Barcelona and Mallorca are beach destinations from June to September, and the Canary Islands are warm all year.
seasons: April–June
Warm and sunny — the best time for cities like Seville, Madrid and Barcelona.
July–August
Peak beach season; inland cities often top 40°C.
September–October
Warm sea and comfortable temperatures across the country.
November–March
Cool on the mainland; winter sun in the Canary Islands.

Thailand.intro: Thailand's cool, dry season from November to February is the best time for most of the country. Watch the coasts: the Andaman side (Phuket, Krabi) is wet from May to October, while the Gulf islands (Koh Samui) get their heaviest rain in October to December.
seasons: November–February
Cool, dry season: the best weather in Bangkok, the north and the Andaman coast.
March–May
Hot season — April is the hottest month, and northern Thailand suffers from smoke haze.
June–October
Rainy season on the Andaman coast; Koh Samui stays relatively dry until October.

Türkiye.intro: Türkiye's best seasons are spring and autumn, when Istanbul is pleasant for walking, Cappadocia's balloons fly in calm skies and the Turquoise Coast has warm seas without peak-summer heat.
seasons: April–June
Mild to warm, ideal for Istanbul, Cappadocia and early beach days.
July–August
Hot beach season on the coast; Istanbul is humid and busy.
September–October
Warm sea and comfortable sightseeing weather.
December–February
Cold, wet winters in Istanbul and snow in Cappadocia.

US National Parks.intro: America's great national parks have very different seasons. Spring and autumn are best for desert parks like Zion and the Grand Canyon, while Yellowstone and much of Yosemite's high country are only fully open from late spring to autumn.
seasons: April–May
Desert parks at their best; Yosemite's waterfalls peak with snowmelt.
June–August
All roads open in Yellowstone and Yosemite, but hot in the desert and very busy.
September–October
Fewer crowds, comfortable temperatures and autumn colours.
November–March
Many roads close in Yellowstone; the Grand Canyon's South Rim stays open year-round.

Vietnam.intro: Vietnam stretches 1,600 km from north to south, so the weather varies: the south is hot with a dry season from December to April, central Vietnam is best from February to August, and the north has a cool winter and hot, wet summer.
seasons: February–April
The best all-round window: mostly dry and warm across the country.
May–August
Great beach weather in central Vietnam; hot and rainy in Hanoi and Saigon.
September–December
Typhoon and flood season on the central coast; pleasant autumn in Hanoi.
